title: Design a Rate Limiter
description: Design a distributed rate limiter that restricts the number of requests a user, IP address, API key, or service can make within a specified time period. The system should protect backend services from abuse, prevent resource exhaustion, and ensure fair usage across clients.
functionalRequirements: Return HTTP 429 when limit is exceeded.
nonFunctionalRequirements: Support millions of requests per second.
highLevelDesign: API Gateway forwards request to Rate Limiter.
Gateway either forwards request or returns HTTP 429.
Metrics are published to monitoring systems.

coreAlgorithms.name: Sliding Window Counter
pros: Good balance of accuracy and memory

recommendedApproach.reason: Provides efficient burst handling while maintaining average request rate limits. Commonly used in large-scale production systems.

deepDiveComponents.responsibility: Intercept and validate requests before backend services.

cachingStrategy: Use local cache fallback during Redis outages.

Support subtitles and multiple audio languages.
highLevelDesign: CDN serves video chunks from nearest location.

cachingStrategy: Use CDN edge caching for video segments.
scalingStrategy: Shard databases by user and content.

tradeoffs.reason: Improves playback speed but increases storage cost.
Better scalability for viewing history and analytics.
Balances user experience and network usage.

title: Design API Gateway
description: Design a highly available and scalable API Gateway that acts as a single entry point for client requests, providing request routing, authentication, authorization, rate limiting, load balancing, monitoring, and resilience features for backend microservices.
functionalRequirements: Route client requests to appropriate backend services.
nonFunctionalRequirements: Support millions of requests per second.

apiDesign.purpose: Create or update API routing rules

highLevelDesign: Service discovery finds healthy backend instances.

architectureComponents.responsibility: Distribute incoming traffic across API Gateway nodes.
Process requests and apply gateway policies.
Validate JWT tokens, API keys, and user identity.
Control request frequency and prevent abuse.
Manage routes, policies, and gateway rules.

recommendedApproach.reason: A stateless gateway cluster with horizontal scaling provides high availability, low latency, and fault tolerance.

cachingStrategy: Use Redis for shared configuration cache.

tradeoffs.decision: Centralized Gateway vs Direct Service Access
tradeoffs.reason: Provides security, monitoring, and consistent policies.
Configuration updates can tolerate small delays.

title: Design Notification System
description: Design a large-scale notification platform that delivers billions of notifications through multiple channels such as push notifications, email, SMS, and in-app notifications. The system should support real-time delivery, reliability, personalization, retries, and user preferences.
functionalRequirements: Allow users to configure notification preferences.
nonFunctionalRequirements: Support billions of notifications per day.
highLevelDesign: Event is published to message queue.
Notification is enriched with template data.
Notification is routed to delivery channel.

architectureComponents.responsibility: Buffer notification events and handle traffic spikes.
Process events and decide delivery strategy.

messageFlow: Event is published to Kafka topic.

recommendedApproach.reason: A queue-based architecture provides scalability, reliability, and decoupling between business services and notification delivery.

cachingStrategy: Use Redis for rate limiting notification sending.
failureHandling: Dead letter queue for permanent failures.

tradeoffs.reason: Improves scalability and prevents blocking business operations.

tradeoffs.decision: Exactly Once vs At Least Once Delivery

tradeoffs.reason: Critical alerts are real-time while marketing notifications can be batched.
